All claims are dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalized claims.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No assessments were due at this explore stage, so I registered new discovery comparisons rather than re-assessing existing claims. The first five proposals test whether the five accepted core dependency patterns persist under genome-copy-number context. High ploidy can amplify, attenuate, or leave unchanged dependency contrasts because of genomic instability, selection strength, and technical noise in CRISPR screens. The WRN-MSI, SMARCA2-SMARCA4, USP7-TP53, and NFE2L2-KEAP1 contrasts are directionally maintained by the signed-estimate convention: for direction -1, a positive estimate means stronger raw dependency; for direction +1, a positive estimate means weaker dependency. The MDM2 low-ploidy proposal complements the accepted high-ploidy MDM2-CDKN2A stratum. The next two MDM2 proposals refine unresolved deletion-structure questions. The TP53-loss/high-copy 9p21 stratum is linked to H158 because it broadens that TP53-loss context beyond MTAP-intact cells and asks whether CDKN2A loss still predicts stronger MDM2 dependency when the 9p21 copy-number profile is not in the low-copy deleted range. The MTAP-intact/high-copy 9p21 stratum tests the broader CDKN2A-MDM2 association when MTAP is intact and low-copy 9p21 deletion is not imposed, helping distinguish a general CDKN2A association from co-deletion-structure artifacts. The final STAT3-MYC proposal probes a biologically motivated receptor/signaling-effector question: MYC amplification may reflect transcriptional programs that cooperate with STAT3 signaling, so MYC-amplified cells could show stronger STAT3 dependency. The alternative is that the effect is null or attenuated. All proposals are dataset-specific associations, not causal or externally generalizable claims. No validation request is made because the validation budget is exhausted and this stage is exploration.","analyze":"No assessments are due at this analyze stage, so I selected twelve already registered, active, untested comparisons to maximize information from the next round of discovery analyses. I used the signed-estimate convention throughout: for direction -1 claims, a positive estimate means the exposed group has the raw more negative, i.e. stronger, dependency score; for direction +1 claims, a positive estimate means weaker dependency. For MDM2, the approximate 10% outcome-magnitude scale remains about 0.027, whereas the accepted core WRN, SMARCA2, USP7, and NFE2L2 associations are very large on their respective dependency-score scales. First, I requested the five low-screen-quality strata H182 through H186. These test whether the accepted core associations remain robust when screen_roc_auc is below the high-quality threshold: WRN by MSI status, SMARCA2 by SMARCA4 loss, USP7 by TP53 loss, NFE2L2 by KEAP1 loss, and MDM2 by CDKN2A loss. Low screen sensitivity is a plausible attenuation source, so concordance in these strata would strengthen internal validity, while attenuation or reversal would be scientifically important. Second, I requested the ploidy robustness strata H187 through H191. These test high-ploidy contexts for WRN-MSI, SMARCA2-SMARCA4, USP7-TP53, and NFE2L2-KEAP1, plus a low-ploidy MDM2-CDKN2A stratum. Because copy-number instability can change selection pressures and technical noise in CRISPR dependency scores, these tests address whether the accepted dependencies are artifacts of a particular ploidy regime. Third, I requested H192 and H193 to refine the unresolved MTAP and 9p21 deletion-structure issue for MDM2. H192 tests CDKN2A loss versus intact MDM2 dependency among TP53-loss tumors whose copy_number_9p21 is not in the low-copy deleted range. This broadens the TP53-loss context after H158 became unresolved because independent validation was wide and crossed null. H193 tests CDKN2A loss versus intact MDM2 dependency among MTAP-intact tumors with non-low-copy copy_number_9p21, asking whether the CDKN2A-MDM2 association is general rather than confined to particular deletion contexts. If both remain positive and above the approximate MDM2 clinical scale, this would support a broader CDKN2A-MDM2 association. If they are small or unstable, it would support context dependence and caution against interpreting CDKN2A as a simple standalone predictor of MDM2 dependency. I prioritized these tests over remaining matched-omics strata, H146, H176-H177, H194, and other deferred comparisons because low-quality screen strata, ploidy strata, and the MDM2 deletion-structure question are more likely to change or constrain the current conclusions. No independent validation is requested because no new validation requests remain available.","appraise":"I used the signed-estimate convention: for direction -1 claims, a positive estimate means the exposed group has the more negative raw dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims, a positive estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. For MDM2 I continued to use the approximate 10% outcome-magnitude scale of about 0.027 dependency-score units used in prior appraisals, while the four core large associations have effects many-fold above their respective clinical scales. H182 tests WRN dependency in MSI-high versus non-MSI cells restricted to lower screen_roc_auc. R158 gives +0.781 (0.730 to 0.832), a very large difference far above zero and the clinical threshold. This confirms that the accepted MSI-high stronger WRN dependency pattern is not confined to high-quality screens. I accept and close H182. H183 tests SMARCA2 dependency by SMARCA4 loss in lower-quality screens. R159 gives +0.775 (0.744 to 0.806), again extremely large and clinically decisive, so H183 is accepted and closed. H184 tests USP7 dependency by TP53 loss under lower screen quality. With direction +1, R160 gives +0.798 (0.764 to 0.831), meaning TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency. This agrees with the validated USP7-TP53 pattern and is accepted/closed. H185 tests NFE2L2 dependency by KEAP1 loss under lower screen quality. R161 gives +0.805 (0.774 to 0.836), meaning KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, consistent with the validated KEAP1-NFE2L2 pattern; accept/closed. H186 tests MDM2 dependency by CDKN2A loss under lower screen quality. R162 gives +0.118 (0.083 to 0.178) before signing? Actually signed estimate is +0.0853 (0.0364 to 0.1342), still far above zero and above the approximate MDM2 clinical threshold, although attenuated relative to high-quality screens. This supports the accepted CDKN2A-to-stronger-MDM2 association even in lower-quality screens; accept/closed. H187 tests WRN-MSI among high ploidy. R163 gives +0.788 (0.732 to 0.844), confirming the effect in a copy-number-instability context; accept/closed. H188 tests SMARCA2-SMARCA4 among high ploidy. R164 gives +0.762 (0.726 to 0.798), very large and consistent; accept/closed. H189 tests USP7-TP53 among high ploidy. R165 gives +0.800 (0.765 to 0.836) under direction +1, i.e. weaker USP7 dependency with TP53 loss; accept/closed. H190 tests NFE2L2-KEAP1 among high ploidy. R166 gives +0.802 (0.763 to 0.842) under direction +1, i.e. weaker NFE2L2 dependency with KEAP1 loss; accept/closed. H191 tests MDM2-CDKN2A among low ploidy. R167 gives +0.147 (0.083 to 0.211), above the MDM2 clinical threshold with a lower bound also above it; accept/closed. These results materially strengthen internal robustness of the accepted core associations across screen quality and ploidy contexts, though they remain dataset-specific associations. H192 asks whether CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency among TP53-loss tumors outside the low-copy_number_9p21 range. R168 is invalid because the exposed cell has only 2 observations (cell_n [2,302]); it cannot support or refute the hypothesis. I leave status unresolved but close investigation because the prespecified cell is too sparse to yield interpretable evidence in this dataset. H193 tests CDKN2A loss among MTAP-intact tumors outside the low-copy 9p21 range. R169 gives a clinically relevant point estimate of +0.118, but the interval (-0.065 to +0.300) crosses zero and the lower bound is well below the clinical threshold, with only 23 exposed observations. This is compatible with a meaningful CDKN2A-MDM2 association, but not sufficient to accept it as scientifically established in this exact non-low-copy, MTAP-intact context. I keep it unresolved and active because targeted refinement or other complementary strata could clarify whether the effect is generally present outside low-copy 9p21 or depends on deletion co-structure. No validation request is made: the run has no remaining new validation requests, and the strongest patterns already have independent validation.","synthesize":"I assessed the due validation for H153 and reassessed H158 in light of its validation result. I continued to use the signed-estimate convention: for direction -1 comparisons a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has the more negative raw dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1 comparisons a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has weaker dependency. For MDM2 the approximate 10 percent outcome-magnitude scale is about 0.027 dependency-score units, while the four core accepted dependencies have effects far above their respective scales. H153 tests CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A intact for MDM2 dependency among TP53-intact tumors with low copy_number_9p21 and MTAP intact. Discovery R132 was +0.113 with interval +0.058 to +0.167. Independent validation R144 was larger, +0.152 with interval +0.061 to +0.244 at the strict validation alpha. Both point estimates and both lower bounds are above zero and above the approximate clinical scale, so I accept and close H153. This strengthens the broader CDKN2A-to-stronger-MDM2 association in a biologically relevant TP53-intact low-9p21 MTAP-intact context. H158 tests the narrower exact context of CDKN2A loss among TP53-loss and MTAP-intact tumors. Discovery R134 was positive, +0.0998 with interval +0.018 to +0.181, but independent validation R157 was smaller and imprecise, +0.0586 with interval -0.071 to +0.188. The validation interval includes no difference, weaker MDM2 dependency, and clinically meaningful stronger dependency. Although the point estimate remains in the expected direction, the combined evidence is not sufficient for this exact subgroup. I downgrade H158 from accepted to unresolved and keep it active because targeted discovery refinements can clarify whether the attenuation reflects TP53-loss context, MTAP co-deletion structure, or small-sample instability. This does not overturn the broader CDKN2A-MDM2 result, which remains supported by H80 overall, H83 under TP53 loss, H141 under TP53-intact low-9p21 validation, and H153 validated here. Final scientific report. The strongest supported dataset-specific findings are five context-specific CRISPR dependency associations. First, MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency. H6 discovery R6 was +0.790 interval +0.760 to +0.819, and independent validation R53 was +0.821 interval +0.766 to +0.877. This pattern is robust across many strata, including library, batch, mutation burden, growth rate, screen quality, ploidy, TP53 status, KRAS status, matched QC eligibility, and other contexts. Second, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. H7 discovery R7 was +0.784 interval +0.765 to +0.803, and validation R39 was +0.801 interval +0.771 to +0.830. This also remains supported across Avana, non-Avana, screen quality, ploidy, TP53-intact, KRAS-mutant, matched RNA/DNA, and co-mutation strata. Third, TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency. H11 discovery R11 was +0.802 interval +0.782 to +0.822, and validation R13 was +0.800 interval +0.769 to +0.832. This pattern persists across multiple genomic and technical strata. Fourth, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency. H17 signed discovery R8 was +0.796 interval +0.776 to +0.816, and validation R26 was +0.791 interval +0.761 to +0.821. Broad stratum support makes this a decisive dataset-specific association. Fifth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. H80 overall discovery R59 was +0.117 interval +0.082 to +0.152, and validation R66 was +0.130 interval +0.078 to +0.182. This is clinically meaningful on the MDM2 scale but much smaller than the four core large associations. It is not merely a generic MTAP-loss effect: MTAP loss alone is mostly null or small, and CDKN2A remains clinically relevant in several validated or near-validated low-9p21 contexts, including H141 and H153. Supported negative and control findings are important. KRAS mutation is not associated with clinically meaningful KRAS dependency, H1 R1 +0.0137 interval -0.0038 to +0.0312. BRAF V600E is not associated with clinically meaningful BRAF dependency, H2 R2 -0.0165 interval -0.0448 to +0.0117. ERBB2 amplification is not associated with ERBB2 dependency, H4 R4 +0.00146 interval -0.0267 to +0.0296. MYC amplification is null for DHX9, RPL11, POLR2A, and KIF18A, H9, H10, H19, and H110. TP53 loss is not clinically meaningful for MDM2, NFE2L2, RPL11, or STAT3 in the predicted stronger-dependency directions, H5, H77, H114, and H151. RB1 loss is not associated with KIF18A, H95. BRCA2 loss is not associated with KIF18A, H20. NF1 loss is not associated with RIT1, KRAS, or STAT3, H72, H73, and H96. PIK3CA mutation is not associated with STAT3, H12. STK11 loss is not associated with SMARCA2, H138. EGFR amplification shows a reverse or null association for STAT3, H174 rejected. Research markers D, E, and F are broadly null across the major dependencies, supporting that the large accepted associations are not artifacts of these constructed role-free assays. Unresolved uncertainty centers on MDM2 deletion structure. H158 is unresolved because its independent validation crosses null. H193 remains unresolved because the point estimate is clinically relevant, +0.118, but the interval crosses zero and exposed cell count is low. These test whether the accepted core associations remain robust when screen_roc_auc is below the high-quality threshold: WRN by MSI status, SMARCA2 by SMARCA4 loss, USP7 by TP53 loss, NFE2L2 by KEAP1 loss, and MDM2 by CDKN2A loss. Because copy-number instability can change selection pressures and technical noise in CRISPR dependency scores, these tests address whether the accepted dependencies are artifacts of a particular ploidy regime. If both remain positive and above the approximate MDM2 clinical scale, this would support a broader CDKN2A-MDM2 association. H182 tests WRN dependency in MSI-high versus non-MSI cells restricted to lower screen_roc_auc. R158 gives +0.781 (0.730 to 0.832), a very large difference far above zero and the clinical threshold. H183 tests SMARCA2 dependency by SMARCA4 loss in lower-quality screens. R159 gives +0.775 (0.744 to 0.806), again extremely large and clinically decisive, so H183 is accepted and closed. H184 tests USP7 dependency by TP53 loss under lower screen quality. With direction +1, R160 gives +0.798 (0.764 to 0.831), meaning TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency. This agrees with the validated USP7-TP53 pattern and is accepted/closed. H185 tests NFE2L2 dependency by KEAP1 loss under lower screen quality. R161 gives +0.805 (0.774 to 0.836), meaning KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, consistent with the validated KEAP1-NFE2L2 pattern; accept/closed. H186 tests MDM2 dependency by CDKN2A loss under lower screen quality. R162 gives +0.118 (0.083 to 0.178) before signing? Actually signed estimate is +0.0853 (0.0364 to 0.1342), still far above zero and above the approximate MDM2 clinical threshold, although attenuated relative to high-quality screens. This supports the accepted CDKN2A-to-stronger-MDM2 association even in lower-quality screens; accept/closed. H187 tests WRN-MSI among high ploidy. R163 gives +0.788 (0.732 to 0.844), confirming the effect in a copy-number-instability context; accept/closed. H188 tests SMARCA2-SMARCA4 among high ploidy. R164 gives +0.762 (0.726 to 0.798), very large and consistent; accept/closed. H189 tests USP7-TP53 among high ploidy. R165 gives +0.800 (0.765 to 0.836) under direction +1, i.e. weaker USP7 dependency with TP53 loss; accept/closed. H190 tests NFE2L2-KEAP1 among high ploidy. R166 gives +0.802 (0.763 to 0.842) under direction +1, i.e. weaker NFE2L2 dependency with KEAP1 loss; accept/closed. H191 tests MDM2-CDKN2A among low ploidy. R167 gives +0.147 (0.083 to 0.211), above the MDM2 clinical threshold with a lower bound also above it; accept/closed. These results materially strengthen internal robustness of the accepted core associations across screen quality and ploidy contexts, though they remain dataset-specific associations. Both point estimates and both lower bounds are above zero and above the approximate clinical scale, so I accept and close H153. This strengthens the broader CDKN2A-to-stronger-MDM2 association in a biologically relevant TP53-intact low-9p21 MTAP-intact context. record.narrative: No assessments are due at this analyze stage, so I used the slot to request twelve new discovery analyses rather than cached comparisons that would reuse existing data. I continued the signed-estimate convention: all selected claims have direction -1, so a positive estimate means the exposed group has a more negative, i.e. stronger, raw dependency score relative to the comparator. For MDM2, I continue to treat a difference around 0.027 dependency-score units as the approximate 10 percent outcome-magnitude clinical threshold, although the four core dependencies have much larger effects on their own scales. The highest-value uncertainty is the structure of the CDKN2A-to-MDM2 dependency association. H80, H82-H84, H92-H93, H100, H107, H127, H132, H141, H153, H157, H171, H173, H186, H188, H190, and H191 broadly support CDKN2A loss as a predictor of stronger MDM2 dependency, but H158 and H193 leave narrower deletion/co-mutation contexts unresolved. Therefore I requested H178 to isolate MTAP loss among TP53-loss CDKN2A-intact cells, H195 to test CDKN2A loss when both TP53 loss and MTAP loss are present, H179 and H180 to split the TP53-loss MTAP-intact context by copy_number_9p21 threshold, H181 to test MTAP loss within CDKN2A-loss TP53-loss low-9p21 cells, and H204 to broaden the low-9p21 TP53-intact stratum beyond the previously validated -0.5 threshold. H172, H200, and H201 test matched-RNA/DNA, batch_b, and 10 percent serum robustness of the MDM2 CDKN2A association. I limited further robustness testing for the already decisive core associations to H203, asking whether the accepted SMARCA4-loss-to-stronger-SMARCA2-dependency pattern persists in ARID1A-loss cells. Finally, H205 and H208 are focused exploratory follow-ups: WRN dependency by BRCA2 loss, which is biologically plausible through DNA repair/helicase relationships, and EGFR dependency by EGFR amplification in an adenocarcinoma TP53-intact stratum, which follows up the borderline unresolved EGFR signal. The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

expectation

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: I assessed all newly delivered results under the signed convention: for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has the stronger raw dependency (more negative score). I did not assess H56 in this stage because it is the duplicate canonical ARID1A-loss SMARCA4 context already represented by H203; assessing the duplicate would violate the canonical-claim rule. H204 is clinically meaningful: CDKN2A loss in a broad low-9p21/TP53-intact context gives R175 +0.127 (0.085 to 0.170), well above the MDM2 clinical scale of about 0.027. This broadens the earlier stricter low-9p21 deletion evidence. H172, H200, and H201 are robustness tests in matched RNA/DNA, batch_b, and 10% serum; R176 +0.113 (0.076 to 0.150), R177 +0.146 (0.065 to 0.226), and R178 +0.114 (0.070 to 0.157) all clear the MDM2 threshold and support the dataset-specific CDKN2A-to-MDM2 association. H203 tests SMARCA4 loss within ARID1A loss; R179 +0.814 (0.767 to 0.862) is decisive, so the SMARCA4/SMARCA2 dependency pattern is not explained away by ARID1A-loss co-occurrence. H178 is rejected: MTAP loss among TP53-loss CDKN2A-intact cells gives R170 -0.013 (-0.067 to 0.040), small and opposite to the predicted stronger-dependency direction, so it does not support a generic MTAP effect in this exact context. H205 is rejected for the exact WRN/BRCA2 hypothesis: R180 -0.0001 (-0.045 to 0.045) is essentially null, with no evidence of clinically meaningful stronger WRN dependency in BRCA2-loss cells. H208 remains borderline unresolved: R181 +0.021 (-0.011 to 0.054) in adenocarcinoma TP53-intact EGFR-dependent tumors has a point estimate below the EGFR clinical scale of about 0.025, but the upper bound includes clinically meaningful values, so the EGFR amplification signal remains unsupported as a stable clinically meaningful effect. H179, H180, H181, and H195 have invalid evidence because at least one comparison cell has fewer than 20 observations. They cannot support or refute their exact sparse hypotheses, so I leave them unresolved but close those exact prespecified contexts; this does not weaken the broader accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 findings. No validation is requested because the new-request validation budget is exhausted.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: I reassessed H158 under the signed convention: direction -1, so a positive estimate means exposed has the more negative raw MDM2 score, i.e. stronger dependency. H158 tests CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A intact among TP53-loss, MTAP-intact tumors. Discovery R134 was clinically meaningful (+0.0998; 95% interval +0.018 to +0.182), but independent validation R157 at the strict validation alpha was smaller and imprecise (+0.0586; interval -0.071 to +0.189). The validation interval includes no difference, clinically meaningful stronger dependency, and clinically meaningful weaker dependency. Therefore the exact TP53-loss MTAP-intact subgroup no longer supports acceptance; I downgrade H158 to unresolved and keep it active for adequately powered discovery refinement. This does not overturn the broader CDKN2A-to-MDM2 dependency association: H80 overall accepted with validated R66, H83 accepted with validated R105, H141 validated, H153 validated, and several broad low-9p21 and MTAP-intact strata accepted. The current report's strongest supported dataset-specific findings remain five context associations: MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency (H6 discovery R6 +0.790; validated R53 +0.821); SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H7 R7 +0.784; validated R39 +0.801); TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency (H11 R11 +0.802; validated R13 +0.800 under direction +1); KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H17 signed R8 +0.796; validated R26 +0.791 under direction +1); and CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency (H80 R59 +0.117; validated R66 +0.130). These are associations in the supplied panel, not causal or external generalizability claims. Supported negative findings include KRAS mutation not clinically meaningful for KRAS dependency (H1 R1), BRAF V600E not clinically meaningful for BRAF dependency (H2 R2), ERBB2 amplification not clinically meaningful for ERBB2 dependency (H4 R4), MYC amplification null for DHX9/RPL11/POLR2A/KIF18A, RB1 loss null for KIF18A, BRCA2 loss null for KIF18A and WRN (H20), NF1 loss null for RIT1/KRAS/STAT3, PIK3CA mutation null for STAT3, STK11 loss null for SMARCA2, and research markers D/E/F broadly null across major dependencies. MTAP loss is not established as a generic MDM2 driver: H81 and H94 are rejected, H178 is rejected in TP53-loss CDKN2A-intact cells, H99 remains active/unresolved, and H158 is now unresolved. EGFR amplification versus EGFR dependency remains borderline unresolved (H3 and related adenocarcinoma strata), with point estimates near but generally below the clinical scale and intervals including null. The most informative next analyses are discovery tests that avoid sparse cells: (i) broaden H158 into TP53-loss MTAP-intact low-9p21 with copy_number_9p21 <= -0.25; (ii) test CDKN2A loss in TP53-loss low-9p21 regardless of MTAP status; (iii) test MTAP loss among CDKN2A-intact broad low-9p21 tumors to separate CDKN2A-specific from broader 9p21 loss; (iv) continue core robustness tests already registered/active in library, batch, matched-QC, and ploidy strata; and (v) refine EGFR amp in TP53-intact adenocarcinoma with KRAS/BRAF/ERBB2 wildtype. Iteration 15/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due at this explore stage. Validation budget is exhausted, so I registered new discovery comparisons that remain adequately powered while directly addressing open mechanistic or robustness questions. I continued the signed-estimate convention: for direction -1 claims, a positive estimate corresponds to a more negative raw dependency score in the exposed group, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims, a positive estimate corresponds to a less negative raw score, i.e. weaker dependency. The approximate 10% clinical effect scale is about 0.025-0.028 for MDM2 and several core scores, although the five accepted core effects are far larger.

The first two proposals focus on the accepted CDKN2A-to-MDM2 dependency association. A broad low-9p21 stratum tests whether the effect is still clinically meaningful across a wider deletion context rather than being tied only to the stricter -0.5 or to MTAP/TP53 exact co-occurrence. This is important because CDKN2A and MTAP are both near 9p21, and prior narrower splits created sparse or unstable cells. The high-Cas9 stratum tests internal screening robustness; concordance would argue against Cas9-activity-dependent artifacts.

The next seven proposals test robustness of accepted core dependencies in culture and genomic-context strata that have not yet been examined for the relevant outcomes: high serum for WRN, USP7, and NFE2L2; low ploidy for USP7, NFE2L2, SMARCA2, and WRN. These complements existing accepted high-ploidy or high-screen-quality results. If these strata remain concordant, the accepted dataset-specific associations are less likely to be artifacts of a single screening condition. If they attenuate, that is scientifically useful context-specificity rather than a failure.

The MYC-expression comparisons test a plausible explanation for the overall null MYC-amplification effects on DHX9 and RPL11: amplification may matter only when MYC transcript output is high. A positive result would support an expression-conditioned hypothesis; a null result in this populated stratum would further weaken the case for MYC-amplification-specific dependency.

The final proposal tests a new pathway hypothesis: EGFR amplification in KRAS-wild-type adenocarcinoma may be associated with stronger KRAS dependency because EGFR signaling lies upstream of the KRAS/MAPK axis. This is a candidate association in this dataset only, not a causal or externally generalizable claim.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: No assessments are due at this analyze stage, and the independent validation budget is exhausted, so I am using this slot to request twelve previously registered, not-yet-run discovery analyses. All selected comparisons are active, untested, and targeted to the main open follow-up questions identified from the accepted core associations and from the unresolved MDM2/9p21/MTAP context. I retained the signed convention: for direction -1 claims, a positive estimate corresponds to more negative raw dependency score in the exposed group, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims, a positive estimate corresponds to less negative raw score, i.e. weaker dependency. H213 and H214 test robustness of the accepted CDKN2A-loss-to-stronger-MDM2-dependency association in a broad low-9p21 stratum and in high-Cas9 screens, avoiding overly sparse exact co-deletion/co-mutation cells. H215-H217 test accepted core effects in high-serum culture: MSI-high WRN, TP53-loss USP7, and KEAP1-loss NFE2L2. H218-H221 test accepted core effects in low-ploidy contexts, complementing previously accepted high-ploidy robustness results. H222-H223 test whether the overall null MYC-amplification effects on DHX9 and RPL11 become clinically meaningful only in the stratum with high MYC expression, a more biologically coherent conditional hypothesis than using amplification alone. H224 tests a new pathway-level candidate: whether EGFR amplification in KRAS-wild-type adenocarcinoma is associated with stronger KRAS dependency, consistent with EGFR signaling acting upstream of the KRAS/MAPK axis. These analyses are internal association tests in the supplied panel; they will be interpreted in light of clinical-scale effect sizes and uncertainty, and no causal or external-generalizability claim will be made from the current dataset.

Iteration 15/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
I assessed all newly delivered discovery results under the signed convention: for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a more negative raw CRISPR dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means a less negative raw score, i.e. weaker dependency. All due results had valid Welch comparisons with both cells containing at least 20 observations.

The MDM2/CDKN2A association remains robust. H213 tests CDKN2A loss in a broad low-9p21 stratum, copy_number_9p21 <= -0.25; R182 is +0.129 (0.091 to 0.167), far above the approximate MDM2 clinical effect scale of about 0.025-0.027. This supports the dataset-specific association without depending on the stricter 9p21 cutpoint or exact MTAP/TP53 splits. H214 tests high Cas9 activity, cas9_activity_pct >= 80; R183 is +0.147 (0.092 to 0.202), again clinically meaningful and consistent with a screening-quality-robust association. I therefore accept and close both exact claims.

The core dependency associations are also robust in high-serum and low-ploidy contexts. H215, R184, gives +0.784 for MSI-high versus non-MSI-high WRN dependency in 10% serum; H221, R190, gives +0.813 in low ploidy <=2.5. H216, R185, gives +0.800 for TP53-loss versus TP53-intact USP7 dependency in 10% serum, interpreted as weaker USP7 dependency with TP53 loss under direction +1; H218, R187, gives +0.820 in low ploidy. H217, R186, gives +0.814 for KEAP1-loss versus KEAP1-intact NFE2L2 dependency in 10% serum, interpreted as weaker NFE2L2 dependency with KEAP1 loss under direction +1; H219, R188, gives +0.791 in low ploidy. H220, R189, gives +0.791 for SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA4-intact SMARCA2 dependency in low ploidy. These are enormous effects relative to the 10% clinical scale and are concordant with previously accepted core associations. They reduce concern that the original effects are confined to high-ploidy, non-Avana, low-quality, or serum-limited screens. I accept and close these exact robustness claims.

The expression-conditioned MYC hypotheses are not supported. H222 tests whether MYC amplification has a clinically meaningful stronger-DHX9 association only when RNaseq MYC expression is high; R191 is -0.016 (-0.048 to +0.017). The interval includes no effect and its upper bound remains below the approximate clinical scale. H223 similarly gives -0.008 (-0.039 to +0.024) for RPL11. Thus restricting to high-MYC expression does not establish the expected MYC-amplification-specific dependency effects; I reject and close both.

H224, EGFR amplification versus KRAS dependency in KRAS-wild-type adenocarcinoma, remains borderline and unresolved. R193 is +0.014 (-0.023 to +0.050). The point estimate is below the approximate clinical scale, but the interval includes clinically meaningful stronger KRAS dependency. I therefore do not accept it as clinically meaningful, but I also cannot reject it without further evidence. It remains active for adequately powered discovery follow-up.

From a critical-reviewer standpoint, these analyses are associations among measured variables in the supplied panel, not causal claims or claims of external generalizability. The strongest accepted findings are supported by very large signed effects and multiple internal strata; the borderline MYC and EGFR results are not promoted because their uncertainty and effect estimates are too small. No validation request is made because the new voluntary validation budget is exhausted.

Iteration 15/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

I continued the signed-estimate convention: for direction -1 claims, a positive estimate corresponds to a more negative raw dependency score in the exposed group, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims, a positive estimate corresponds to a less negative raw score, i.e. weaker dependency. The approximate 10% clinical effect scale is about 0.025-0.028 for MDM2 and several core scores, although the five accepted core effects are far larger.\n\nThe first two proposals focus on the accepted CDKN2A-to-MDM2 dependency association. A broad low-9p21 stratum tests whether the effect is still clinically meaningful across a wider deletion context rather than being tied only to the stricter -0.5 or to MTAP/TP53 exact co-occurrence. This is important because CDKN2A and MTAP are both near 9p21, and prior narrower splits created sparse or unstable cells. The high-Cas9 stratum tests internal screening robustness; concordance would argue against Cas9-activity-dependent artifacts.\n\nThe next seven proposals test robustness of accepted core dependencies in culture and genomic-context strata that have not yet been examined for the relevant outcomes: high serum for WRN, USP7, and NFE2L2; low ploidy for USP7, NFE2L2, SMARCA2, and WRN. These complements existing accepted high-ploidy or high-screen-quality results. If these strata remain concordant, the accepted dataset-specific associations are less likely to be artifacts of a single screening condition. If they attenuate, that is scientifically useful context-specificity rather than a failure.\n\nThe MYC-expression comparisons test a plausible explanation for the overall null MYC-amplification effects on DHX9 and RPL11: amplification may matter only when MYC transcript output is high. H213 tests CDKN2A loss in a broad low-9p21 stratum, copy_number_9p21 <= -0.25; R182 is +0.129 (0.091 to 0.167), far above the approximate MDM2 clinical effect scale of about 0.025-0.027. Discovery R134 was clinically meaningful (+0.0998; 95% interval +0.018 to +0.182), but independent validation R157 at the strict validation alpha was smaller and imprecise (+0.0586; interval -0.071 to +0.189). The validation interval includes no difference, clinically meaningful stronger dependency, and clinically meaningful weaker dependency. This does not overturn the broader CDKN2A-to-MDM2 dependency association: H80 overall accepted with validated R66, H83 accepted with validated R105, H141 validated, H153 validated, and several broad low-9p21 and MTAP-intact strata accepted. The current report's strongest supported dataset-specific findings remain five context associations: MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency (H6 discovery R6 +0.790; validated R53 +0.821); SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H7 R7 +0.784; validated R39 +0.801); TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency (H11 R11 +0.802; validated R13 +0.800 under direction +1); KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H17 signed R8 +0.796; validated R26 +0.791 under direction +1); and CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency (H80 R59 +0.117; validated R66 +0.130). record.narrative:
No independent validation deadlines were listed and the voluntary validation budget is exhausted. I therefore completed a synthesis assessment of the existing independent validation evidence and finalized the supported conclusions. The signed convention remains: for direction -1 claims a positive estimate means the exposed group has a more negative raw dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims a positive estimate means a less negative raw score, i.e. weaker dependency.

SUPPORTED CORE DATASET-SPECIFIC ASSOCIATIONS. Five associations are supported by large discovery effects and independent internal validation, and each is many-fold above the approximate 10 percent clinical effect scale. First, MSI-high lineages show much stronger WRN dependency: H6 R6 +0.790, 95 percent discovery interval +0.760 to +0.819; validation R53 +0.821, interval +0.766 to +0.877. Second, SMARCA4 loss shows much stronger SMARCA2 dependency: H7 R7 +0.784, +0.765 to +0.803; validation R39 +0.801, +0.771 to +0.830. Third, TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency under direction +1: H11 R11 +0.802, +0.782 to +0.822; validation R13 +0.800, +0.769 to +0.832. Fourth, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency under direction +1: H17 signed R8 +0.796, +0.776 to +0.816; validation R26 +0.791, +0.761 to +0.821. Fifth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: H80 R59 +0.117, +0.082 to +0.152; validation R66 +0.130, +0.078 to +0.182. The CDKN2A-MDM2 effect is smaller than the four core effects but still several-fold above the clinical threshold and is robust in many independent strata.

ROBUSTNESS. The core associations remain concordant in library, screen-quality, batch, ploidy, serum, matched-QC, and co-mutation strata. The accepted exact strata for CDKN2A-MDM2 include TP53-intact and TP53-loss broad contexts, low-9p21 contexts, MTAP-intact broad contexts, and low-9p21 MTAP-intact contexts. Several of these were validated: H83, H141, H153, and H80. Some exact MTAP-loss strata are less stable at validation: H85 validation R92 has point +0.096 but lower -0.002, and H132 validation R118 has point +0.108 with lower -0.024. I retained them as accepted because the discovery intervals are strong and clinically meaningful, but they should not be presented as the primary CDKN2A-MDM2 evidence. The broader CDKN2A-MDM2 conclusion does not depend on these exact MTAP-loss or exact triple-context cells.

UNRESOLVED EXACT MDM2/MTAP CONTEXTS. H158, CDKN2A loss in TP53-loss MTAP-intact tumors, was clinically meaningful in discovery R134 +0.0998, +0.018 to +0.181, but independent validation R157 was smaller and imprecise +0.059, -0.071 to +0.189. I keep H158 unresolved and active. H99, MTAP loss among CDKN2A-loss tumors, remains active unresolved with discovery R84 +0.064, -0.025 to +0.153. These exact contexts need adequately powered broad strata such as active H209, H210, and H211 rather than sparse triple splits.

NEGATIVE FINDINGS. Several intuitive biomarker-dependency hypotheses are rejected in this panel because intervals are near zero and point estimates are below the clinical threshold. KRAS mutation is not a clinically meaningful predictor of KRAS dependency: H1 R1 +0.014, -0.004 to +0.031. BRAF V600E is not clinically meaningful for BRAF dependency: H2 R2 -0.017, -0.045 to +0.012. ERBB2 amplification is not clinically meaningful for ERBB2 dependency: H4 R4 +0.0015. MYC amplification is not clinically meaningful for DHX9, RPL11, POLR2A, or KIF18A, including a high-MYC-expression stratum: H222 R191 -0.016, -0.048 to +0.017 and H223 R192 -0.008, -0.039 to +0.024. RB1 loss is not clinically meaningful for KIF18A: H95 R75 +0.008. BRCA2 loss is null for KIF18A and WRN: H20 R25 and H205 R180. NF1 loss is null for RIT1, KRAS, and STAT3: H72 R64, H73 R65, H96 R76. PIK3CA mutation is null for STAT3: H12 R12. STK11 loss is null for KRAS dependency and SMARCA2: H54 R38 and H138 R117. MTAP loss is not established as a generic MDM2 driver: H81 R98, H94 R74, and H178 R170 are rejected, while H99 and H158 remain unresolved. Research markers D, E, and F are broadly null across the major dependencies; validated example is H42 R60 -0.008 and R79 -0.001 for USP7.

BORDERLINE UNRESOLVED SIGNALS. EGFR amplification versus EGFR dependency remains borderline unresolved. H3 R3 +0.025, -0.000 to +0.050 is near but not sufficiently above the clinical threshold; adenocarcinoma and driver-wild-type strata H71 R52 +0.021, -0.017 to +0.059 and H208 R181 +0.021, -0.011 to +0.054 remain similar. H224, EGFR amplification versus KRAS dependency in KRAS-wild-type adenocarcinoma, is also borderline: R193 +0.014, -0.023 to +0.050. ERBB2 amplification versus STAT3 H175 R156 +0.022, -0.015 to +0.059 is borderline active. These are not promoted to accepted claims.

NEXT ANALYSES. The most informative next analyses are discovery comparisons that avoid sparse cells and address the two main open uncertainties. First, run active H209, H210, and H211 to separate CDKN2A-specific MDM2 effects from broader 9p21 or MTAP context using broad low-9p21 strata. Second, run H212 and the newly proposed interaction of EGFR amplification by KRAS-mutant status on EGFR dependency to determine whether the borderline EGFR signal is concentrated in KRAS-wild-type adenocarcinoma; also run H224 and active EGFR/STAT3/other unresolved predictors if cells allow. Third, complete active core robustness claims where power is adequate, including batch, KY-library, and matched-QC strata, but no new validation can be requested because the validation budget is exhausted.

GENERALIZABILITY AND CAUSALITY. All accepted statements are associations among measured variables in the supplied panel, supported by internal validation. They are not proof that the measured alteration causes the dependency, and they are not external clinical generalizability claims. In particular, the large WRN and SMARCA2 effects are strong evidence of context-specific dependency patterns, but causal mechanism requires direct perturbation or independent experimental replication.

No assessments are due at this analyze stage, and the independent validation budget is exhausted, so I am requesting 12 previously registered, active, not-yet-run discovery comparisons. All are existing claim references and have not received direct evidence. I retained the signed convention: for direction -1 claims, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a more negative raw CRISPR dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims, a positive estimate means a less negative raw score, i.e. weaker dependency.

The selected analyses target the main open questions without relying on validation. First, I completed selected core-robustness contexts: H146 tests SMARCA4-loss-associated SMARCA2 dependency within TP53-loss tumors, and H207 tests MSI-high WRN dependency in high-aneuploidy tumors. H236 tests whether the accepted SMARCA4-loss effect on SMARCA2 is modified by ARID1A loss, a broad co-alteration context rather than a sparse exact triple split.

Second, I retained the two main MDM2/9p21/MTAP follow-up questions that use broad strata rather than very sparse co-deletion cells: H210 tests CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency among TP53-loss tumors with copy_number_9p21 <= -0.25, and H211 tests whether MTAP loss is associated with MDM2 dependency among CDKN2A-intact tumors in the same broad low-9p21 stratum. These help distinguish a CDKN2A-specific association from broader 9p21/MTAP co-deletion context.

Third, I targeted the borderline EGFR amplification signal with H212, a driver-wild-type, TP53-intact adenocarcinoma context, and H225, an interaction of EGFR amplification by KRAS mutation status. These ask whether the EGFR association is concentrated in genomically cleaner contexts or modified by KRAS status.

Fourth, I tested biologically motivated pathway bypass predictors: H229, H230, and H231 test whether PIK3CA mutation or PTEN loss is associated with weaker KRAS, BRAF, or EGFR dependency, respectively, under direction +1. Finally, I broadened exploration with two untested predictor associations: H232 tests APC mutation versus STAT3 dependency, and H233 tests RB1 loss versus SMARCA2 dependency.
